line: One JSON line of the listener's log, in CloudWatch group /superci-pull/listener: {"msg":"tl","v":1,"ev":<name>,"t":<event time, RFC 3339 UTC>,"t_ms":<the same in epoch milliseconds>,"boot":<the listener process>,"eid":<unique to the line>,<fields>}. Append-only: one line per fact, written where the fact happens, with no counter or aggregate. t is when the fact happened by the clock of its source; the log's own time is when it was written. The log ships at least once, so a reader keeps one line of each eid, and takes the first of each (inst, name) for a machine's mark, which a machine resends until the listener answers. Fields are only ever added; a reader ignores the ones it does not know, and v changes when a field's meaning does. Every table and number the timeline tool prints is derived from these lines and the GitHub API, and can be rebuilt from them.

keys.job: job (GitHub's job GUID) joins every listener event of one job, with the set; run and name tie it to GitHub's REST job. rr, the runner request id, is 0 in the assigned, started and completed messages this listener is sent, so no join uses it
keys.machine: inst (EC2 instance id) joins every event of one machine; a job meets its machine at job.started (runner = <set>-<inst>)
keys.process: boot names the listener process that wrote the line; listener.start opens a boot

job.available.what: GitHub never sends this to this listener (0 of 7,023 messages on Nov 25); kept for a listener that is sent it

job.assigned.what: the listener's first sight of a job: GitHub assigned it to the set; t is when the listener saw it, queue_time is GitHub's

job.started.what: the runner took the job; queue_ms is the listener's view of the wait since GitHub queued it

job.record.what: the one record of a finished job, written once when JobCompleted arrives (a listener restart forgets which jobs it recorded, so a completion GitHub redelivers after one adds a line with the same job, and a reader keeps the first): the message's times and result joined with the machine that ran it and its estimated cost. t is the job's finish by GitHub's clock. conclusion is GitHub's REST word (success, failure, cancelled; a timed_out job reads failure). queue_ms is queue_time to start_time and wall_ms start_time to finish_time, the gate's queue wait and wall time. warm says the machine was launched before the job was queued. usd is the machine's estimated cost from its launch to the finish and busy_usd the part of it while the job ran; the rest is boot and idle. The machine's fields (region to busy_usd) are absent when the listener held no machine of the runner. partial says the job's start is unknown (its completion arrived after a restart, with no start time in the message): queue_ms, wall_ms and busy_usd are then left out, not zero. workflow_ref names the workflow file and the branch

machine.launched.what: EC2 answered the CreateFleet that started the machine; requested is when the call began

machine.ended.what: the listener asked EC2 to terminate the machine

machine.notice.what: AWS gave notice it takes the spot machine back

jit.ask.what: the machine's first ask for its runner (the identity document posted); verdict is wait while the registration budget or readiness holds it

jit.issued.what: the runner was registered, tagged and its config left

jit.refused.what: no config left: end (told 410), exists, refused (GitHub's cap), failed, withheld

boot.start.what: boot.sh began; val is the OS uptime in seconds

doc.got.what: the identity document was read from the metadata service

jit.sent.what: the first ask for the runner left the machine

jit.answered.what: the machine got a final answer to its ask; val is the HTTP code

runner.online.what: the runner printed Listening for Jobs

job.done.what: the runner printed the job's result

job.got.what: dispatch mode: the agent took its job from the dispatcher

worker.start.what: dispatch mode: the agent started Runner.Worker

worker.exit.what: dispatch mode: Runner.Worker exited; val is its exit status

runner.exit.what: run.sh returned; val is its exit status

ec2.state.what: EC2's state-change notification (pending, running, shutting-down, terminated), in group /superci-pull/ec2-state of each region (run deploy/timeline.sh), time to the second

jit.granted.what: the ask that was granted: the registration token wait ended; waited_ms since its first ask, polls the asks it took (the machine asks every 3 s)

jit.wait.what: a machine still told to wait for its runner, written every 30 s of the wait (jit.granted comes only at its end); why is the budget's denial (window, tokens, throttled, blind), issuing or not_ready

listener.start.what: a listener process began; every later line carries its boot

launch.decision.what: why a launch round asked EC2 for n machines: the set's snapshot, and the limit the registration budget left across the sets

pool.target.what: a set's pool and what it holds, every state log; the burst..chosen fields are the pool rule's, added by pull-wait

machine.retired.what: the listener ends a machine on its own judgment: stuck, overdue, retire (idle runner removed), shed

hydrate.start.what: pre-hydration of the machine's caches (pull-prehydrate): began

hydrate.done.what: pre-hydration of the machine's caches (pull-prehydrate): ended; val is bytes:entries

readset.start.what: a size with a read set (readsets/<label>.list) began reading the image files its jobs read; offset_ms is from the hydration's start

readset.done.what: the read set's files were read into the page cache: full, or stopped by the job; such a machine reads no whole root

preread.start.what: the machine began reading its root volume's snapshot blocks (so no job's first read of one waits on the snapshot); offset_ms is from the hydration's start

preread.done.what: the read of the root volume ended; val is full when it read all of it and stopped when the job started first

rewarm.done.what: after the pre-read, the walk of the hydrated and image trees ended: full, or stopped by the job

pin.done.what: the hydrated checkout's files were locked in memory (pullcache pin), so a job's memory pressure cannot push them out of the page cache; val is files:MB, with :capped when a cap stopped it, :stopped when the machine refused a lock and :failedN for N files it could not lock, or late (no summary within a second) or failed (the pinner died)

warm.done.what: after the walk, the binaries jobs start were read into the page cache: full, or stopped by the job

warm.ready.what: a dispatch machine asked for its job: its warm was done, or its uptime reached the cap (boot.sh)

cache.restore.what: the cache daemon served a restore; val is hit:<bytes>:<ms>:<key> or miss:0:0:<key>, the key percent-encoded

cache.save.what: the cache daemon finished a save; val is saved:<bytes>:<ms>:<key>

jit.claim.what: the claim a grant takes before it registers a runner (pull-fence): result is taken, refused (another grant holds it) or error (the claim store failed); claim_ms how long it took
